findings.title: Tier 1 case CCP-RESEALED-DECISION-LAUNDERING never reseals its forgery, so the product refuses it under a different code and the case fails
findings.evidence: RUN-TIER1.py sets forged['decision']['decision']='REFUSE' only, then requires the refusal text to contain CCP_ADMISSIBILITY_DECISION_INVALID. ccp_admissibility._validate_decision_shape runs first: the control decision carries gateway_disposition SEPARATE_GATEWAY_AUTHORIZATION_REQUIRED, which is only valid for ADMIT, so it refuses with CCP_ADMISSIBILITY_GATEWAY_DISPOSITION_INVALID (line 854) before the decision-equality check (line 892) is reached; the decision_root would also mismatch. refuses() requires the exact code and returns False, giving PREDICATE_FALSE. The builder's own unit test test_ccp_binding_holds_nonadmitted_transition does the full reseal (gateway disposition and decision_root) and expects DECISION_INVALID; it passed in replay.
findings.consequence: Case 010 failed on a refused forgery; case 017 (authority ceiling) failed only as the aggregate. Your HOLD_FOR_REPAIR carries no evidence of a CCP bypass. Same class as R27-01.
findings.repair: Make the court mirror the unit test (set gateway_disposition to NOT_ELIGIBLE_FOR_EFFECT and recompute decision_root), or accept any CCP_ADMISSIBILITY_* refusal; keep an unresealed variant as a separate case expecting the shape refusal.
